papers.title: Domain dynamics within the PriA DNA helicase regulate DNA replication restart.
papers.summary: In E. coli, the PriA helicase restarts stalled replication forks. The authors show lagging-strand structure controls the position of PriA's cysteine-rich region: single-stranded DNA permits a rotated PriACRR state that encircles the strand and recruits PriB, whereas duplex lagging strands do not. Mutant analyses support a regulatory switch coupling fork architecture to PriA activity.

papers.title: BaCas12a3 represents a new subtype of type V CRISPR effector with collateral activity toward tRNA.
papers.summary: BaCas12a3, a new type V CRISPR effector from Bacteroides, arrests host growth without double-strand DNA breaks. It is an RNA-activated nuclease that cleaves the 3' terminal CCA of tRNAs. Cryo-EM reveals a bilobed architecture with a tRNA-loading domain beside the RuvC site, opening on target binding to enable specific tRNA cleavage.

papers.title: The stability of m6A-marked transcripts is linked to cell identity in planarians.
papers.summary: Using multiplexed direct RNA sequencing, the authors mapped ~72,200 m6A sites in planarians, enriched near stop codons and excluded from coding regions, consistent with exon-junction-complex-mediated exclusion. Writer knockdown caused cell-type-specific stability changes: intestinal transcripts destabilized, neoblast transcripts stabilized. m6A thus stabilizes mRNAs in differentiated cells but promotes decay in stem cells, shaping cell identity.

papers.title: MeCP2 MBD-ID module: a unified DNA/RNA binding interface disrupted in Rett syndrome.
papers.summary: The MeCP2 methyl-CpG binding domain (MBD) and intervening domain (ID) function as a synergistic unit: the ID boosts methylated-DNA affinity ~35-fold, and together they form a high-affinity RNA-binding module whose binding precludes DNA binding. Rett syndrome ID mutations selectively weaken RNA and non-methylated DNA binding, disrupting this competitive nucleic-acid balance and explaining disease etiology.

papers.title: MERGE-RNA: a physics-based model to predict RNA secondary structure ensembles with chemical probing.
papers.summary: MERGE-RNA models RNA as structural ensembles by explicitly modeling the physics of chemical-probing experiments (e.g., DMS), using maximum-entropy to predict thermodynamic populations consistent with data. It outperforms standard pseudo-free-energy methods, recovers NMR-resolved conformations and ligand-induced population shifts of the Vibrio adenine riboswitch, and deconvolves transient intermediates invisible to few-structure enumeration approaches.

papers.title: pH-dependent allosteric remodeling of a bacterial riboswitch couples alkaline activation to metal sensing.
papers.summary: The E. coli alx yybP-ykoY riboswitch couples manganese sensing to alkalinity. Single-molecule FRET shows Mn2+ stabilizes a docked three-way-junction conformation, and alkaline pH sensitizes metal-dependent folding. Simulations identify a loop that at low pH allosterically disrupts the Mn2+-binding state; in vivo reporters confirm both loop and metal core are required for pH-dependent activation.

papers.title: CD81 drives immune evasion in radioresistant glioblastoma by blocking selective autophagic degradation of CD274/PD-L1.
papers.summary: CD81 is highly expressed in radioresistant glioblastoma and drives immune evasion. CD81 binds CD274/PD-L1 via its extracellular loop and recruits USP14, erasing K63 ubiquitination at K280 and blocking p62-dependent autophagic degradation of PD-L1. CD81 depletion restores PD-L1 autophagy, increases CD8+ T-cell infiltration and cytotoxicity, and augments anti-PD-1 therapy combined with radiotherapy.

papers.title: The spindle-associated antisense RNA ARHGEF17-AS1 functionally contributes to mitotic spindle integrity.
papers.summary: ARHGEF17-AS1 is a metaphase-enriched antisense lncRNA localizing to the mitotic spindle. It interacts with RPS3 and dynein, supporting RPS3 recruitment to spindle poles and RPS3-dynein association. Depletion lowers RPS3 abundance, reduces RNF10 expression, abolishes mitotic RPS3 monoubiquitination at K214, and disrupts spindle organization, delaying mitotic progression.

papers.title: An amygdaloreticular pathway promotes motor programs of ingestion.
papers.summary: Central amygdala neurons collateralize to the parabrachial nucleus and pontine/medullary premotor fields controlling orofacial movement. Terminal activity correlates with licking regardless of metabolic need or palatability. Optogenetic stimulation evokes overeating, consumption of inedible objects, or ingestion-like behaviors without targets, indicating this pathway flexibly recruits a consummatory motor state rather than simply suppressing satiety.

papers.title: Processing of lysophosphatidylcholines by ExoU secreted by P. aeruginosa leads to inflammasome activation and cell death.
papers.summary: In chronic cystic fibrosis isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, type III secretion genes show elevated polymorphism and poor expression. The T3SS phospholipase ExoU extensively remodels the infected cell lipidome, raising lysophosphatidylcholine species that activate NF-kB and MAPK pathways and drive inflammasome-mediated cell death; this process is inhibited by lysophosphatidylcholine acyltransferase 3 (LPCAT3).

papers.title: SDCBP competes with CBL to stabilize PES1 and promote c-Myc translation in ESCC tumorigenesis.
papers.summary: SDCBP binds PES1 and competitively disrupts its CBL-mediated ubiquitination, stabilizing PES1, enhancing pre-rRNA processing and c-Myc synthesis. SDCBP ablation suppresses tumors in a 4NQO murine model. Cyclic RGD lipid nanoparticles delivering SDCBP antisense oligonucleotides silence the axis in a tumor-targeted manner and inhibit patient-derived xenograft growth without apparent toxicity.

papers.title: A USP28-BRD4 axis contributes to the acceleration of breast cancer growth by hyperglycemia.
papers.summary: Hyperglycemia stabilizes BRD4 to accelerate breast cancer growth. The deubiquitinase USP28 interacts with and deubiquitinates BRD4, requiring USP28 acetylation at K702 by KAT8, antagonized by SIRT1. Diabetes lowers NAD+, weakening SIRT1, increasing USP28 acetylation and BRD4 stability. Disrupting this USP28-BRD4 axis abrogates hyperglycemia-driven tumor growth in functional studies.

papers.title: PAG supports T cell immune synapse function by binding to actin.
papers.summary: PAG, a T-cell adaptor mediating PD-1 inhibitory signaling, binds actin via its C-terminal PDZ-binding motif; PAG and actin dynamics synchronize during immune synapse maturation. Motif mutation disrupts this interaction, impairing synapse formation, stability, and function. In hypersensitivity and cancer models, T cells expressing mutant PAG show reduced immune responses and cytotoxicity.

papers.title: Dishevelled drives disassembly of primary cilia through an unusual PDZ domain-mediated binding mode with Girdin-L.
papers.summary: Proximity labeling identified DAPLE and Girdin-L as high-affinity ligands of the Dvl2 PDZ domain via extended C-terminal motifs. Dvl2's PDZ domain clusters around basal bodies and recruits girdin, and this interaction promotes primary cilia disassembly, accelerated by Wnt5a. Girdin-L is thus a functionally relevant Dishevelled PDZ ligand regulating cilium disassembly.

papers.title: Crystal structure and biochemical analysis of the polyester-degrading carboxylesterase SM0281 from the symbiotic legume-associated rhizobacterium Sinorhizobium (Ensifer) meliloti.
papers.summary: SM0281 from Sinorhizobium meliloti is a carboxylesterase preferring medium-chain monoesters, tolerant of varied pH, salts, and solvents, and cold-active. It hydrolyzes the PET model substrate 3PET to MHET with activity on PET, PCL, and PLA. Its 2.46 A crystal structure shows a lid domain over the catalytic serine with PEG bound in a tunnel cavity.

papers.title: γ-Glutamylcysteine alleviates hypertension and vascular remodeling in SHR by suppressing oxidative stress through Keap1 S-glutathionylation.
papers.journal: Redox report : communications in free radical research
papers.summary: In spontaneously hypertensive rats, gamma-glutamylcysteine lowered blood pressure and prevented arterial medial thickening, while inhibiting vascular smooth muscle cell migration, proliferation, and phenotypic switching. Mechanistically, it induced Keap1 S-glutathionylation, disrupting Keap1-NRF2 interaction and promoting NRF2 nuclear translocation; NRF2 inhibition with ML385 abolished these protective effects in vivo and in vitro.

papers.title: Structural organization of TAM receptor ectodomains.
papers.summary: An X-ray structure of the MERTK ectodomain reveals a highly curved conformation stabilized by N-glycans, confirmed flexible in solution by SAXS. Comparisons across TAM receptors show distinct curvatures (TYRO3 most bent, AXL straightest), and a head-to-tail IG2-FNIIIB intermolecular contact suggests clustering mechanisms potentially guiding receptor-specific functions in phagocytosis and immune regulation.

papers.title: Alr2204-Alr2205 form a functional modular thioredoxin system that enhances oxidative stress tolerance in cyanobacteria.
papers.summary: In Anabaena, Alr2204 (thioredoxin reductase) and Alr2205 (atypical thioredoxin) form a cognate redox pair functionally analogous to chloroplast NTRC. Alr2204 is FAD-associated and NADPH-dependent, donates electrons to Alr2205, and overexpression enhances oxidative stress resistance. Co-expression elevates reduced 2-Cys-Prx levels and sustains its peroxidase activity, linking thioredoxin modulation to stress tolerance.

papers.title: METTL1-mediated m7G modification regulates hair follicle cycle via the HOXC13/FOXN1/DSG4 axis.
papers.summary: Keratinocyte-specific METTL1 knockout causes hair follicle dysplasia, impaired regeneration, and disrupted adhesion, while knock-in accelerates hair regeneration. Beyond tRNA effects, METTL1 deficiency destabilizes HOXC13 mRNA through internal m7G modification, downregulating the HOXC13/FOXN1/DSG4 axis. m7G methylation thus post-transcriptionally controls a key transcriptional circuit governing hair follicle morphogenesis and cycling.

papers.title: Olfactomedin 4 marks progenitor cells that give rise to the secretory cell lineage in the mouse cervix.
papers.summary: Lineage tracing identifies Olfactomedin 4 as a marker of KRT8+TRP63- progenitors in the mouse cervix that give rise to goblet cells, while TRP63+ progenitors generate keratinocytes. Two independent progenitor populations are delineated by postnatal day 15. OLFM4+ progenitors proliferate in early gestation, and progesterone promotes their differentiation, mirroring human cervicovaginal epithelium organization.

papers.title: Conserved C-terminal residues adjacent to the canonical PDX1 homeodomain are required for chromatin occupancy and pancreas development.
papers.summary: A conserved intrinsically disordered region at PDX1's C-terminus (residues 207-223) is required for pancreas development. Mice lacking this region show pancreatic hypoplasia and impaired endocrine differentiation despite normal PDX1 levels, with loss of chromatin occupancy at target genes and reduced insulin promoter activation. The requirement maps to four conserved residues (207-210).

papers.title: 5q31 duplications encompassing PURA are associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder.
papers.journal: European journal of human genetics : EJHG
papers.summary: Ten individuals with 5q31 duplications encompassing PURA define a novel genomic disorder: developmental delay with mild-to-moderate intellectual disability, milder than the reciprocal deletion syndrome. The minimal 215 kb overlap contains only PURA, which is upregulated at mRNA and protein levels. PURA overexpression impairs neuronal morphology, reducing dendritic arborization and spine density in mice.

papers.title: The deubiquitinase USP5 mediates anti-PD-L1 resistance in breast cancer by stabilizing FOXM1 to upregulate Nectin2.
papers.summary: USP5 is upregulated in breast cancer and stabilizes FOXM1 via deubiquitination, increasing Nectin2 expression and resistance to CD8+ T-cell killing. USP5 knockdown or pharmacological inhibition with G9 synergizes with anti-PD-L1 therapy to suppress tumor growth, an effect reversed by Nectin2 overexpression, positioning USP5 as a target for overcoming immunotherapy resistance.

papers.title: Evolution of freshwater reproduction in a marine fish: Evidence from genetics and otolith microchemistry.
papers.journal: Evolution; international journal of organic evolution
papers.summary: Otolith microchemistry confirms European flounders in Lake Pulmanki complete their entire life cycle in freshwater, a first for the species; nearby fjord fish are also largely freshwater-born. Genome-wide differentiation is weak, but 77 SNPs across 35 genes show strong interchromosomal linkage disequilibrium, suggesting epistatic selection on allelic combinations underlying freshwater reproduction.

papers.title: Genomic Diversity and Population Structure of Semi-Domesticated Reindeer populations in Southern Norway and wild reindeer from Iceland.
papers.summary: A chromosome-level genome assembly for Norwegian semi-domesticated tundra reindeer (2.54 Gb, 39,855 genes) enabled resequencing of 175 Norwegian and 28 Icelandic animals. Norwegian populations show low differentiation and similar diversity, while Iceland's founders show reduced diversity from founder effects and long-term isolation. Recent inbreeding is low across all populations.

papers.title: BRCA1-mediated transcriptional repression of FABP3 - Implications for breast cancer progression and chemosensitivity.
papers.summary: FABP3 is identified as a novel BRCA1-repressed target gene: functional BRCA1 represses the FABP3 promoter, while mutant BRCA1 cell lines show elevated FABP3 restored by wild-type BRCA1. FABP3 overexpression promotes proliferation, clonogenicity, and migration yet confers chemosensitivity. High FABP3/BRCA1 ratios correlate with reduced survival, linking BRCA1 loss to tumor aggressiveness.

papers.title: A context-dependent modulatory role for eIF6 in acquired resistance to vemurafenib in melanoma.
papers.summary: In vemurafenib-resistant melanoma cells, eIF6 is upregulated alongside dysregulated MAPK, PI3K-AKT, metabolic, and ribosome biogenesis pathways. eIF6 silencing reduces proliferation and partially restores vemurafenib sensitivity, while overexpression increases drug sensitivity irrespective of BRAF status via mTOR and MAPK modulation, revealing a context-dependent link between translation control and targeted-therapy response.

papers.title: RA-PLA: Retrieval-augmented graph convolutional networks for protein-ligand binding affinity prediction.
papers.summary: RA-PLA retrieves hard protein-ligand pairs and integrates them through semi-supervised graph convolutional networks with per-query fine-tuning. It outperforms state-of-the-art methods on PDBbind, DAVIS, KIBA, and BindingDB (e.g., DAVIS CI 0.952; PDBbind CI improved 11.4%), and achieves 15.5% average cold-target AUPR gains. Ablations confirm retrieval and end-to-end learning are both essential.

papers.title: Proteomic and lipidomic characterization of Hemipyrellia ligurriens larval extracts using LC-MS/MS and GC-MS: Identification of putative antimicrobial molecules and preliminary functional assessment.
papers.summary: First integrative proteomic and lipidomic characterization of Hemipyrellia ligurriens blow fly larvae: 9,444 proteins in whole-body extracts and 10,977 in excretory-secretory products, with compartment-specific diversity. Defensin-like, diptericin-like, and attacin-like antimicrobial peptides, lysozymes, and 26 fatty acids were identified. Extracts showed selective, moderate antibacterial activity without keratinocyte cytotoxicity, supporting antimicrobial potential.

papers.title: BRD proteins in human retroviral infection: emerging evidence from HIV-1 and future perspectives for HTLV-1.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes bromodomain protein roles in human retroviral infection. BRD9, an ncBAF complex component, recently emerged as a regulator of HIV-1 latency through proviral transcription control, while BRD4 and other BET proteins regulate transcription, latency, and oncogenic signaling in HIV-1 and HTLV-1. Direct BRD9-HTLV-1 evidence remains absent; research directions are proposed.

papers.title: Identification and gene expression profiling of toll genes in the potato psyllid (Bactericera cockerelli) in response to 'Candidatus liberibacter solanacearum'.
papers.summary: The potato psyllid genome encodes six Toll receptors and ten pathway genes. Five Toll receptors are induced by the entomopathogenic fungus Beauveria bassiana. Responses to 'Candidatus Liberibacter solanacearum' are haplotype-specific: Toll like-1 and Toll-7 upregulate during LsoB acquisition, only Toll-7 for LsoA, with distinct spatzle induction; persistent infection does not alter Toll expression.

papers.title: Identification and functional annotation of drought-induced molecular pathways in sugarcane using suppression subtractive hybridization.
papers.summary: Suppression subtractive hybridization identified 452 and 625 drought-responsive transcripts in two sugarcane genotypes. Drought tolerance associated with coumarin-mediated responses in AS 04-1687 versus ABA signaling and ascorbate biosynthesis in TSGS 20-24. MYB, NAC, bZIP, SPL, and WRKY regulators were common, with additional JAZ-mediated defense coordination in TSGS 20-24, informing drought-resistance gene discovery.

papers.title: Dysregulated polyamine metabolism in neurological disorders: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities.
papers.summary: This review integrates evidence linking polyamine (putrescine, spermidine, spermine) dysregulation to neurological disease via four mechanisms: autophagy, oxidative stress, proteostasis, and neuroinflammation. Alzheimer's, Parkinson's (including ATP13A2-associated Kufor-Rakeb), ALS, epilepsy, and Snyder-Robinson syndrome are covered. Therapeutic strategies include spermidine administration and enzyme/transporter modulation, but translation requires CNS biomarkers and blood-brain barrier optimization.

papers.title: The role of the adipose-derived Stromal Vascular Fraction (SVF) secretome as an immunomodulator in the treatment of chronic inflammatory diseases through NF-κB and macrophage reprogramming.
papers.summary: This review proposes that the freshly isolated stromal vascular fraction (SVF) secretome modulates inflammation by inhibiting IKK phosphorylation, stabilizing IkB-alpha to block NF-kB nuclear translocation, and promoting metabolic shift toward oxidative phosphorylation supporting M2 macrophage polarization via STAT6/PPAR-gamma. It recommends standardized GMP isolation methods and evaluation of donor-dependent biochemical variability.

papers.title: Mutational Spectrum of DMD Gene Variants and Cascade Screening Outcomes in the Central-Eastern Black Sea Region of Türkiye: A Single-Centre Retrospective Study.
papers.summary: Among 47 individuals tested for DMD variants at a Turkish center (2022-2026), 19 carried pathogenic variants: ten probands and nine cascade-detected heterozygotes. Diagnostic yield was 30.3% and cascade carrier detection 64.3%. Seven deletions (six in the distal hotspot, exons 45-55) and two sequence variants were found; no proband qualified for approved exon-skipping therapy.

papers.title: Pathologic and immunohistochemical findings in sea bass (Dicentrarchus labrax) naturally infected with Aeromonas veronii biovar veronii.
papers.journal: Biotechnic & histochemistry : official publication of the Biological Stain Commission
papers.summary: In farmed European sea bass naturally infected with Aeromonas veronii biovar veronii, granulomas affecting skin, spleen, kidney, and liver arise from epithelioid macrophage clusters and progress through five stages to caseous necrosis. Immunohistochemistry localized bacterial antigens within necrotic regions and macrophage cytoplasm, identifying macrophages as primary host cells enabling intra- and inter-tissue dissemination.
